New: a pull request review window with a chat and comments you choose to post.

What's new

- Click a pull request in the notch to open the review window. The left side lists the pull requests you review, with each one's review and pipeline status. The right side shows the selected one: branch, pipeline, commit, verdict, and a note when commits were pushed after the review.
- Chat about the pull request the way you would in Claude Code. Each message continues the review's own Claude Code session, so it already knows the code and the findings. The chat is read only: it can read the code and answer, and it never posts.
- Findings become comment cards: severity, file and line (opens the line on Bitbucket), text you can edit, and an Add / Skip switch. Blocking and Should fix start on Add, Nits on Skip. Ask the chat to draft a new comment or reword one, and it updates the cards. Draft comments builds cards for reviews made before this version.
- The comments already on the pull request are listed, and a card that repeats one on the same line is marked.
- Post N comments posts the cards switched on, after a confirm that lists them: each on its file and line, or as a general comment when it has no line. Posted cards are marked and never posted twice.
- Re-review, View report, Open on Bitbucket, Request changes and Approve are in the window's header, with the same rules as before. The notch row keeps a short review status.

Fixes

- The review status and actions under a pull request row no longer get cut off.

Limits

- Posting comments, Approve and Request changes need the Bitbucket API token with write access to pull requests (Setup → Pull requests).
- One chat reply at a time per pull request; replies take a few seconds.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

After upgrading, the app is signed ad hoc, so macOS forgets Microphone, Input Monitoring and Accessibility: remove AI Notch from each list in System Settings → Privacy & Security, add it again, then quit and reopen the app.

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later (dictation: macOS 26).
